issue.title: Tests that plant hardcoded PIDs (11111/22222) in workspace claims never stub pid_is_thread, so a colliding host TID makes those claims look dead
issue.description:
PROPOSED BY phase bead sase-um.9.5.4 (note #7) during epic sase-um.9.5 ("Complete the
interrupted sase-um.9 release-gate landing"), routed to a task by sase-um.9.5.land on
2026-08-29. The epic fixed the one node that actually failed; this bead covers the
remaining sites, which have the same latent defect and have simply not collided yet.

## The mechanism, already reproduced

`sase.core.process_identity.pid_is_thread(pid)` returns True when `pid` names a thread
ID rather than a process. `is_process_alive` uses it, so a fixture that plants an
arbitrary integer PID is silently treated as dead whenever that integer happens to be a
live TID on the host. Linux hands out TIDs from the same number space as PIDs, so a busy
CI runner with many threads makes low, memorable constants like 11111 and 22222
plausible live TIDs.

That is not hypothetical. Full CI run 33240119114, job 99068560982 (3.12 coverage leg),
SHA c1a5b36f5: `tests/test_running_agents_snapshot.py::test_list_all_agents_includes_done_and_failed`
failed because the fixture agent TS_ACE_RUN_RETRIED_CHILD (pid 33333) was missing from
`list_all_agents`. `pid_is_thread(33333)` was true on that runner. Commit ca7692ee3
stubbed `pid_is_thread` in that file's snapshot process fixture and added a colliding
`/proc` regression; the same leg was green afterwards.

## Sites still exposed

`grep -rn "pid=11111\|pid=22222" tests/` finds hardcoded claim PIDs with no
`pid_is_thread` stub in at least:

- tests/test_running_field_transfer.py (pid=11111, from_pid=11111, to_pid=22222)
- tests/test_running_field_release.py
- tests/test_running_field_claim.py
- tests/test_running_field_allocation.py
- tests/test_running_field_adopt_runner_workspace.py
- tests/test_axe_run_agent_runner_deferred_workspace_claim.py

Only tests/test_running_agents_snapshot.py, tests/test_agent_user_kill.py, and
tests/test_process_identity.py reference `pid_is_thread` at all today.

These are workspace-claim tests, so the failure mode is the mirror image of the snapshot
one: a claim whose PID is judged dead gets reclaimed or dropped, and the assertion about
contention or occupancy silently inverts. Expect an intermittent, host-dependent CI-only
failure rather than a crash.

## Scope

Give these fixtures the same treatment ca7692ee3 gave the snapshot fixture -- a shared
stub or fixture is preferable to repeating it per file -- so a planted PID is never
mistaken for a live thread. Consider whether the better fix is at the seam instead:
making the fixtures allocate PIDs that cannot collide, or having `is_process_alive`
distinguish "PID was never a real process here" from "PID is a thread", so no future
test has to remember the stub.

task_type_fields.impact: Intermittent, host-dependent CI-only failures in the workspace-claim suites: a claim whose planted PID collides with a live TID is judged dead, so contention and occupancy assertions invert. Each one costs a full CI cycle to attribute, as this class already did once during epic sase-um.9.5.

Fixed there by ca7692ee3 (stub pid_is_thread in the snapshot process fixture + colliding /proc regression). grep -rn "pid=11111|pid=22222" tests/ shows the listed files still plant PIDs with no stub.

payload.description: Same process_identity/pid-filtering seam: a worker changing how planted PIDs are judged alive will touch the tests sase-uw reports broken by the pid-recycling guard.
